claims.text: Embedding nanoscale Ag particles in CoCrFeNi will promote formation of an Ag-rich film during sliding.
The Ag-rich film will lower the coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Ag-rich film will lower wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting material is a powder-metallurgy CoCrFeNi alloy without Ag reinforcement.
Ag nanoparticles dispersed in CoCrFeNi will migrate toward the wear interface under heating and sliding.
Migrated Ag nanoparticles will coalesce into a continuous film at the wear interface.
Silver has sufficiently low shear strength to provide lubrication in the proposed sliding system.
Silver has sufficiently high ductility to form a ductile interfacial layer during sliding.
The Ag-derived interfacial layer will act as a self-lubricating layer.
The self-lubricating Ag layer will reduce friction and protect the underlying CoCrFeNi substrate from wear.
The underlying CoCrFeNi substrate is hard relative to the ductile Ag-rich layer.
The Ag-reinforced composite will have significantly lower friction coefficients than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The Ag-reinforced composite will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The friction and wear benefits will remain robust across the entire range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits higher friction and accelerated wear under comparable tribological conditions.
The proposed benefits will persist under controlled oxidizing conditions and controlled loads up to 800 °C.
Ag agglomeration at extended high temperatures may compromise tribological performance.
Rapid Ag depletion at extended high temperatures may compromise tribological performance.
